idiom_name: Fluent @Field with a Codable type stored in a JSON column
implementation_notes: Fluent's SQL drivers store nested Codable values in JSON columns: declare @Field(key: "details") var details: OrderDetails and the value is persisted as a JSON document (the migration declares it with .dictionary or .array(of:)), decoded on read without a hand-written mapper. Filtering inside such fields is documented as limited, so attributes that are queried, sorted or constrained stay top-level columns. On Core Data the same decision is a transformable attribute with a secure transformer rather than a raw JSON string field.
pitfalls: Nested Codable fields cannot be filtered or sorted like columns (Fluent states the limitation), so queryable attributes must stay out of the document.
Fluent models are reference types with mutable property wrappers; sharing an instance across tasks or event loops races - decode per request and keep values immutable.
A non-optional @Field with willSet/didSet observers that read the current value traps at runtime (documented by Vapor); use @OptionalField for nullable state.
